slides.headline: Find the arrest. Two detectives, one man.
slides.sub: William Powell Frith, The Railway Station, 1862

slides.headline: Paddington
slides.text: London's Paddington Station, 1862. Hundreds of travellers rush for the train. Frith painted each one as a little story.

slides.headline: The arrest
slides.text: On the right, two detectives have just caught a man as he climbs into a carriage. His escape is over.

slides.headline: Real detectives
slides.text: The detectives were real: Frith asked two well-known Scotland Yard officers to pose for him in his studio.

slides.headline: The wedding
slides.text: In the middle, a bride and groom set off on their honeymoon, surrounded by friends waving them goodbye.

slides.headline: The family
slides.text: Frith painted himself and his own family in the crowd, seeing the boys off to school.

slides.headline: Little dramas
slides.text: A cab driver argues about the fare, porters rush with luggage. Everyone here has a small drama of their own.

slides.headline: A sensation
slides.text: Crowds paid to see the painting in London, and Frith was paid a fortune for it, including the rights to sell prints.

slides.headline: Which story?
slides.text: One arrest, one wedding, one goodbye. If you were on this platform, which stranger's story would you follow?
